# arngz across desks: the desk's desktop count, no launches, and a reload after the window filter fails

cc's design for hv decision 23 (3), 25 Nov 2026, from vc's brief of the same day. Evidence: `~/Devel/scratch/utilz-vc/arngz-analysis-20261125.md`. Code read at main 032e33b4. For 2.15.0, by hv decision 24.

r2 takes the 14 points of ic's second read (`~/Devel/scratch/utilz-ic/desks1125-read/read-r1.md`, 3bee9805): the contract's names and rows, the toasts a reload clears, what an app that is not installed reads as, the extra desktops a run leaves, the names of the apps not running, and the words for the code. r3 takes vc's three notes on A (vc's DESIGN READ of ddb85bef): a proof of each removal in place of the order guard, the cost of a miss, and the probe on every display. r3 also adds WP D, by hv decision 26. r4 takes ic's read of r3 (`~/Devel/scratch/utilz-ic/desks1125-read/read-r2.md`, 7192976d): the resumed step's frame, the pause's `still`, the give-up's fix, the note's rounding, and three nits. r5 records the build of B, C and D, which vc landed at df4f5e74 after one booked run (Runs, 2). Five criteria name log_test in place of engine_test, by vc's word of 25 Nov 2026. C's ends and D's ends now give the code's words. A's code waits on the probe.

- STca1b7f9's objective is hv decision 13's: apps with windows on several desktops, and the route past a full-screen desktop. Its open parts wait on the spike.
- These four changes wait on no spike result. So this thread can land before STca1b7f9's spike code.

The WPs:

- **A** (WP 88504807), each display keeps the desk's desktop count: M. Its code waits on the probe.
- **B** (WP 35219619), apply never launches an app: S.
- **C** (WP a45b3aeb), a reload and one retry after the window filter fails: S.

- ic's toast parts for A, B, C and D (help/arngz.md's Toasts section, and AC-88504807.8, AC-35219619.6, AC-a45b3aeb.8 and AC-4cb617e2.6): S, on the same branch after cc's code, as for STca1b7f9.

## A. Extra empty desktops are removed before any move

### The plan (pure, plan.lua)

- For each desk display, `have` is the matched screen's user desktops (`P.user_spaces`) and `need` is the desk's. When `have > need`, the plan removes up to `have - need` of that screen's empty desktops.
- **Empty**: observe read the desktop with no `windows_error`, and every window it lists is also listed on another space (`P.listings`). A window on every space holds no desktop.
- **Which ones**: the set whose removal leaves the most desk entries with a window of their app already on their desktop. A tie removes the later desktops first, then keeps the shown one.
  - Why: at a plug-in, macOS puts one new empty desktop first on the monitor, before the desktops it carries back (vc's analysis, Cause 1). Removing that one lines the carried desktops up with the desk, so their windows need no move. "Remove from the end" removes the wrong one there.
- With fewer empty desktops than the excess, the plan removes the ones the score keeps. The report notes that the display keeps more desktops than the desk names, and which of them hold windows. The note counts against nothing.
- A new op, `remove_space` {screen, space, ordinal, path, reason}. `ordinal` is the desktop's place among its display's user desktops, as a move's is. The order is remove_space, create_space, then moves and places. No display needs both, since removal is `have > need` and creation is `need > have`.
- diff's DESCRIBE says "remove empty space <ordinal> of <screen>".
- The plan's moves are planned against the world without the removed desktops. So `diff` and `apply --dry-run` show what apply will do.
- Never a full-screen space, a desktop of a screen the desk does not match, or a display's only desktop.

### The cost of a miss (vc's note (2))

A removal that takes another desktop despite the proof is found by the readback. That desktop's windows go where macOS puts them: the probe's P4 measures where, on macOS 27, and design.md's Runs records it. The run goes on. The replan reads the world, and the moves put those windows on their desk's desktops. A window that a move cannot carry stays where macOS put it, and the report names it. The display keeps the extra empty desktop, and `finished.extra` counts it. The display is never short of a desktop the desk needs, since a removal is planned only where it has more than the desk names.

### Each removal is proven first

`hs.spaces.removeSpace` finds its Mission Control tile by the desktop's place in the live list: `count` is its index in `spacesForScreen`, then `mcSpacesList[count]` (Hammerspoon's `spaces.lua`, removeSpace, after line 821). The live list can part from Mission Control's order (`P.order_spaces`, measured 16 Oct 2026). Then the call removes another desktop.

r1 removed only where the live order equalled the order observe took. vc's note (1): after a display change, observe takes the live order, so that guard passes by default in the plug-in case that A exists for. r3 puts a proof in its place, which holds whatever com.apple.spaces records.

- `hs.spaces.gotoSpace` finds its tile by the same index: `count` from `spacesForScreen`, then `mcSpacesList[count]`, then AXPress (spaces.lua, gotoSpace, after line 754).
- So before each removal, the engine calls `gotoSpace(target)` and reads back `activeSpaceOnScreen`. The display must show the target. Then the tile at the target's index is the target.
- Then `gotoSpace` the desktop that takes the target's place, and read it back, since removeSpace refuses a shown desktop.
- The live list must be the same, id for id, at the proof and just before `removeSpace`, so removeSpace presses the same index.
- A proof that shows another desktop stops removals on that display. The display's extra empty desktops are noted and left, uncounted, and `finished.extra` counts them.
- The cost: two more Mission Control openings for each removal. Removals are rare: a desk that is already right removes none.

The readback after the removal (step 4 below) stays as the second check.

### Execute (arngz.lua, `exec_remove_space`, in prepare's callback before the creates)

1. Read again: the desktop is on the screen, is a user desktop, and is empty. If not, the result is "not removed", with why, and the run goes on.
2. The proof: `gotoSpace(target)`, read back that the display shows it, then `gotoSpace` the desktop that takes its place (the next user desktop that stays, else the one before), and read that back. A proof that fails stops removals on that display.
3. Read the live list again: it must equal the proof's, id for id. Then `removeSpace(id, true)`. Read back `spacesForScreen` until the id is gone, with the create's tries (`M.CREATE_SPACE_TRIES`) and its stop on the Dock's error (`P.space_error_final`). The Dock's error binds creates and removes alike, through the one `ctx.dock_failed`.
4. The readback must show exactly the one id gone and every other id still listed. If another id went, the op fails and names both ids, with the fix "check the desktops on <display> in Mission Control, then run arngz apply again", and no later removal on any display is tried. The run goes on, because the replan reads the world again before any move.
5. Then the `created` wait reads the world, and the replan plans the moves from it with `no_remove` (a second plan never removes).

Mission Control opens and closes once for each removal, as it does for each create today. To open it once for all of them is STca1b7f9 WP6's create part, which waits on M2. When that lands, it takes the removals too.

No new flag. `--no-create` keeps its meaning, and no `--no-remove` is added. help's `--no-create` row says "do not create missing desktops; apply still removes extra empty ones", and help's example with it says the same. `diff` shows each removal first.

### The probe first (vc's brief: a short live test on macOS 27)

`~/Devel/scratch/utilz-cc/desks1125/probe/probe.zsh` and `probe.lua` beside it, for vc to read before any run. hv runs `zsh ~/Devel/scratch/utilz-cc/desks1125/probe/probe.zsh` in the same Desk slot as spike v3, after it. The probe moves no window and needs no hands. Each step is read back and timed, with the load.

P1 to P3 run on every display attached, the built-in first, then each monitor (vc's note (3)):

- **P1**: add two desktops at the end of the display's list. Record what `windowsForSpace` lists for each, which is what "empty" reads as on macOS 27.
- **P2**: prove the first of the two as the engine will (show it, read back, show the desktop before it, read back), then remove it while it is neither shown nor last. Check that exactly that id went.
- **P3**: show the second, and ask to remove it: expect "cannot remove a currently active user space". Show the one before it, remove the second, and check that exactly it went.
- Then show the desktop the display showed at the start.

On the built-in alone, with hv's hands for one step:

- **P4**: add a desktop and show it. hv opens a new TextEdit window there (File > New). The probe shows the desktop before it, removes the one with the window, and reads where the window went. Then it closes that window. This is the cost of a miss, measured (vc's note (2)).

Every display's live order, observe's order and its source, and com.apple.spaces' record are logged at the start, after each display's P1 to P3, and at the end (vc's note (3)). Any desktop the probe added and could not remove is named, for hv to remove by hand.

If P2 or P3 takes another id on any display, or a proof shows another desktop, WP A is not built as written, and the design comes back to vc.

### Contract (progress.md, on cc's word and ic's)

- `planned`: `removes`, beside `creates`.
- `step`: kind `remove`, as a create's is `create`, with `display` and `desktop`. `desktop` is its ordinal on its display when the step begins, so a second removal on one display has a lower ordinal than it had in the plan.
- `step`'s row names every kind the engine sends: "create, remove, move, place or recheck".
- `waiting`: the wait after the desktop edits is for "desktop changes", in place of "new desktops".
- `finished`: `removed` (desktops removed), beside `created`. And `extra`: the user desktops the run leaves beyond the desk's count on the displays it matched, for any reason (no empty one, a proof that failed, or a removal not done), read from the end's observe by a pure P.extra_desktops.

## B. apply never launches an app

- **Plan**: an app that is not running is a `not_running` op, in the first plan and in the replan. It is reported and uncounted. An app that was running when apply began and is not running now stays `gone`, which fails, as today: it quit while the run moved its windows.
- **Report**: the entry's outcome is `not running`. It counts against nothing in apply's exit and in diff's (`P.plan_exit`), as an uncounted unseen does. diff's DESCRIBE says "not running <bundle>", in place of not_launched's "not launching <bundle>".
- **An app that is not installed** reads as `not running`, with exit 0. LaunchServices does not know it, so `own_id` keeps the desk's spelling and `applicationsForBundleID` finds nothing. A word of its own would need a LaunchServices read for each entry, and nothing acts on the difference. help says "not running, or not installed".
- **Removed**: the `launch` op, `exec_launch`, `PHASE.launch` and `PHASE.launched`, `M.LAUNCH_TIMEOUT`, `P.launch_verdict`, `P.unsettled_launches`, `claimable_window` (launch is its one caller), `ctx.launched` and `options.launched`, the `gone` arm for an app this apply launched, the outcome `launched and placed`, and the `not_launched` op.
- `skipped` then has no source (a failed launch, or `--no-launch`). The tally drops `skipped` and gains `not_running`.
- **CLI**: `--no-launch` goes, from apply's options, the request's `no_launch`, the log's options, the usage line and help. No caller passes it: Menuz's desk items run `arngz apply "$MENUZ_ITEM"`, and Molt-matts names no arngz flag. A person who passes it gets apply's unknown-option refusal, exit 2.
- **help/arngz.md**: apply's step 4, the outcomes, the exit codes, the options table and the example say the same.
- **Contract**: `planned` drops `launches`. `waiting` drops "launched apps". `finished` drops `skipped` and gains `not_running` (the count) and `not_running_apps` (their names as one string, eg "Teams, Slack"). `first_outcome` is "failed" or "unseen" only: a not-running entry is uncounted, so it is never `first`. The toast's "Skipped: " label is ic's to change, with AC-322a6511.9's toast_test arms.

## C. A reload and one retry after the window filter fails

The trigger: Hammerspoon's window filter failed on a read that a run's answer came from (`world.window_filter` is not "ran"). Run 20261123T135029Z-82958 failed at `hs/uielement.lua:134`.

### The engine

- The request carries `may_reload`, true on the CLI's first try.
- **apply, first try**: a failed filter at the start read (`PHASE.inventory`) refuses before anything changes, with kind `reload` and the filter's words. A failed filter on a later read that leaves an entry unseen lets the run finish, and its response carries `reload` with the words.
- **apply, second try**: runs as today. The fix of each unseen entry is new: "arngz reloaded Hammerspoon's config and its window filter failed again: quit Hammerspoon, open it again, then run arngz again".
- **discover, first try**: a failed filter refuses with kind `reload`. Second try: it refuses with kind `refused`, and nothing is saved. A desk read without the filter drops the windows on desktops not shown, and `--save --force` writes the whole desk.
- **A new engine verb, `reload`**. It is refused while `arngz_running` is set, which means another run is live. Otherwise it sets `arngz_running` to the reload, so a request in the next moment is refused. Then it sets `arngz_reloading`, schedules `hs.reload()` on a short timer, and answers at once.
- What to do is pure (`P.reload_reason` in plan.lua). The engine carries it.

### The CLI (one function, for apply, auto's apply and discover)

1. A response with kind `reload`, or with a `reload` field, makes the CLI ask the `reload` verb.
2. The CLI polls until Hammerspoon answers from a new state (`arngz_reloading` unset), up to `ARNGZ_RELOAD_TIMEOUT` (a `seconds_setting`, default 30 s).
3. It sends the same request once more, with `may_reload` false and `after_reload_of` (the first run's id) for the run log.
4. One reload per command. The second answer is the command's answer. Before its report, the CLI prints one line: "arngz: Hammerspoon's window filter failed (<where>), so arngz reloaded Hammerspoon's config and ran <verb> again".

The other ends:

- **The reload refused** (a run is live): no reload. The engine says "<a run> is running (asked for at <time>)", where <a run> is "an apply" or "a reload". The first answer stands, with the fix "another arngz run is live; run it again when it has finished". The CLI says "arngz: <the filter's words>, and Hammerspoon's config was not reloaded: <the refusal>".
- **Hammerspoon not back in time**: exit 1, "arngz: after the reload of its config, Hammerspoon did not answer within N s; its response is kept at <path>; fix: open Hammerspoon and read its console".
- **A retry refused after an apply that ran**: exit 1, with the refusal's words. The first try may have moved windows, and exit 2 says that nothing changed.
- **diff and apply --dry-run** change nothing, so they never reload. They say the filter failed, with today's fix.
- Each step goes in the run log through `log_record`: the reload asked, back after N s, or not back.

### What a reload costs

It runs hv's `~/.hammerspoon/init.lua` again, which loads hs.ipc alone, by vc's read. It drops arngz's display watcher, and the next engine call starts it again. So the quiet gate waits its 5 s from the new watcher's start before the retry reads. It also drops `arngz_toast` and its canvases, so the first run's Finished goes when the reload runs, and the retry's Starting draws a new toast. That is why the first Finished says what comes next, and not its counts.

### Contract

- `finished` gains `reload`: true when this answer asks the CLI to reload Hammerspoon and run again, which it does only when the request carried `may_reload`. The engine sends `finished` before the CLI acts.
- `start` carries `after_reload_of` on the retry: the first run's id, under the request's own name for it.
- The toasts are ic's: a `finished` with `reload` says that it reloads and runs again, and a run with `after_reload_of` says "(after a reload)".
- A reload refused, or a Hammerspoon that does not come back, leaves the first Finished saying that it reloads. The CLI's exit is then not 0, so Menuz's notice carries the CLI's words (progress.md, rule 7).

## D. A pause when the pointer moves, then the move goes on (hv decision 26)

Today a pointer more than ABORT_PX (40 px) from where arngz put it is the person taking it back (`hand:check`). The stop ends every move after it: runs 20261123T103906Z-92295 and 20261125T031819Z-63492 left 14 entries "not tried". hv picked "Pause, then go on".

- **What happens to a held window**: arngz lets go of the button at once, as run_legs does today. The window stays where the release left it: on the desktop its display showed at that moment, part-way through a carry, or part-way along a drag.
- **The pause is a phase**: `still`, which reads the pointer every POLL_SECONDS (0.25 s) on a timer, as `quiet` reads the displays. So Hammerspoon's run loop turns and the toast can show the pause. Nothing sleeps inside a callback.
- **How long "still" is**: the pointer stays within STILL_PX (4 px) of one point for STILL_SECONDS (2 s), with no mouse button and no modifier key held (`hands_free`). The verdict is pure: `P.still_verdict`, as `P.quiet_verdict` is.
- **Then the move goes on**: the paused op runs again from the start, planned again from where its window is now (`move_plan` reads `window_home`). Each display's shown desktop is read again first, since the person may have switched one. A window the person put on its target needs no legs, and its readback says so.
- **When a pause gives up**: after PAUSE_LIMIT (30 s) with no still 2 s. Then the moves end as today: the paused move fails with the stop's words and "the pointer did not stay still for 2 s within 30 s", with the fix "keep your hands off the mouse and keyboard until arngz finishes, then run arngz apply again", and every later move is "not tried".
- **A run pauses at most MAX_PAUSES (3) times.** The fourth time the pointer is taken, the moves end as today, with "arngz had paused for the pointer 3 times, the most one run pauses" and the give-up's fix. So a person who is working gets the machine back in a bounded time.
- **Which ops**: any op whose legs the pointer stopped: a move, or a place that had to show its desktop first (`show_desktop`). A place itself uses `setFrame`, not the pointer, as today.
- **Unchanged**: the start. `take_hand` still refuses a held button or modifier before the first move. The resume takes the pointer through `take_hand` too, and its refusal ends the moves with its words and the give-up's fix.
- **Contract**: `waiting` gains `for` "the pointer to be still", with `seconds` PAUSE_LIMIT and `still` STILL_SECONDS. The resumed op's `step` goes out again, with the same `i` and `n`, and, for a move, the window's frame as it is now (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`), since the release left it part-way. `finished` gains `paused` (how many times the run paused). A move that paused and then took has the note "(paused <n> s for the pointer)", where <n> is the whole seconds from the stop to the resume, rounded up, so a pause is never "0 s". The note counts against nothing. The toasts are ic's.

## Not in hv's picks

Cause 2 of vc's analysis, windows a held pointer cannot carry (ChatGPT, Screen Sharing, Teams' title bar once), gets no code: hv decision 26 rules that the layout is enough. ChatGPT and Claude share one desktop in every desk, and when both must move, arngz moves Claude and names ChatGPT for a move by hand. Cause 3, the pointer moved mid-run, is WP D.

  - `AC-88504807.2` (test): The plan removes none where a display has no excess, from a desktop with a window that only it lists, on a full-screen space, or on a screen the desk does not match. Each case that leaves an extra desktop says so, uncounted. plan_test.

## Runs

1. The probe, in spike v3's slot, with hv at the keyboard (light lane). Not run yet: it waits for hv's next "ready".
2. The suites in one booking with the driver's path: arngz.bats, engine.bats and toast.bats (bats lane). As built, B, C and D ran first, without A. Run 01M896PTJKN7AJY4ME52ZFZ5RX, at 4a976767 with the driver `desks1125/run-desks1125.sh` (b4940b54): 194 of 194 ok. Its base leg, over 5cb2c180, was red at each new arm's own assertion, 12 of 13, and the 13th was the one arm named GREEN_AT_BASE in advance. ic's toast leg gave its 28 checks as named. An earlier run, 01M894G2XDVTR6MREEB3E8K3H9, found three faults, all in the tests, which 4a976767 fixed. vc landed B, C and D at df4f5e74. A's code gets its own booked run after the probe.
3. One live run with hv at the keyboard: apply after a plug-in and after an unplug (A), a desk with an app that is not running (B), and a move during which hv takes the pointer and lets go (D). The filter's failure cannot be made on demand, so C's live proof is the first time it comes up, and its arms in the suites carry it until then. Not run yet.
